facts.fact: read_sav/read_dta accept a file-like OBJECT; the first parameter is named filename_path

DTA requires a real file descriptor because ReadStat maps its input: a pure BytesIO is accepted for SAV but REJECTED for DTA with 'This version of the file format is not supported'. The view must therefore expose fileno() over the application's own open.

Reusing one broker object across two row_offset parses FAILS for DTA (ReadStat requires position zero). Reusing one VIEW OBJECT fails identically. Calling view() again — which rewinds the same open — succeeds. This is why the governed loop issues a fresh view per chunk over ONE physical open.
read_file_in_chunks works over a file-like for SAV but NOT for DTA, so the governed chunk route is an explicit row_offset/row_limit loop.
row_offset semantics over a file-like are IDENTICAL to the path baseline: row_offset=2, row_limit=2 returned rows [3.0, 4.0] on both, and the returned index resets to [0,1] in both.

usecols reduces the RESULT columns but does NOT reduce physical reads. Measured on a 12-column / 200-row SAV of 20,159 bytes on disk: a full read and usecols=["c00"] issued an IDENTICAL 278 read calls and 20,659 bytes. The selected route is a genuine LOGICAL selected-read account; the claim that unselected columns were never physically read is NOT enforceable by this library and is not made.
